newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer, other metals steady.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer, other metals steady.

text.p: Gold prices on Monday morning retained gains made last Friday when the dollar, the U.S. stock market and the bond market all lost ground, traders said.
The advance on the New York close was limited, however, and some dealers said they were awaiting the start of U.S. trading to determine whether or not the market would pursue its rally.
"It is not entirely clear whether this was short covering or there was some fresh buying coming into gold on Friday," one analyst said.
Gold was fixed at $326.20 per ounce, against $323.70 on Friday and a close then of $324.60/$325.10, which caught the beginning of the New York-driven rally.
Little progress was made from the New York cash close of $326.90/$327.40 in Asia, where upcoming holidays in Japan limited interest and Hong Kong dealing was largely short covering.

"What was happening elsewhere played a major role in the gold market on Friday," said one market participant, referring to the 156-point fall in the Dow and the losses sustained by the dollar and the U.S. long bond.
A four percent downward move on the Tokyo stock market earlier on Monday also helped gold retain its gains from Friday.
"If there is a re-allocation of funds going on (from the stock markets into gold and elsewhere) it is difficult to know what these people's targets in gold would be," a dealer said.
In the market's current nervous and choppy state, a five or six dollar move in an afternoon would not be surprising, he added.
Even so, the upside looked limited to $340.00 in the medium term. More immediately, $327.00-$328.00 could prove tempting numbers at which to take profits.
Silver's response did not last the weekend. It was quoted at $4.39/$4.41, down a cent and apparently consolidating.
The arrival of Russian platinum and palladium in Tokyo on Friday took very little of the heat out of the PGM (platinum group metals) markets.
"A major concern is the size of the short positions on Tocom (Tokyo's precious metals futures market)," said one dealer.
Russia was out of the market as a supplier of platinum and palladium through the first six months of this year as it adjusted to a series of personnel and administrative changes.
Platinum was quoted at $441.00/$446.00, down a dollar from Friday, and palladium was down $0.75 at $232.00/$235.00.
